Print a study or trajectory preview

Source: R/print.R
print.c2t_study.Rd

Display a compact summary without changing study settings or trajectory data. A study remains an environment, and trajectories remain a data frame.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'c2t_study'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'c2t_trajectories'
print(x, ..., n = 6L)

Arguments

x

A study returned by cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration() or trajectories returned by createTrajectories().

...

Further arguments passed to the data-frame preview's print method. Unused when printing a study.

n

Maximum number of trajectory rows to preview. A non-negative whole number; defaults to six.

Value

The supplied object, invisibly.

Details

The trajectory summary counts patients and distinct clinical labels present in the returned rows. START and EXIT are boundary rows; OUT OF COHORT rows are unresolved cycles. These labels are excluded from the clinical-state count. Merged labels count as distinct states. Episodic output also counts distinct patient-episode pairs and includes episode_id in the preview.

The preview shows patient identifiers, state labels, start and end dates, and time in cohort. All columns remain available through normal data-frame operations. Use as.data.frame(x) for the ordinary full data-frame display or View(x) to inspect the table. Column subsets without the trajectory's patient, label or date columns use ordinary data-frame printing.

Inspect a study's individual settings with x$settingName, or all settings with as.list(x, all.names = TRUE). Printing does not read patient files or change the saved study.
